title: Best Rooftop Bar in Manta, Ecuador: An Honest 2026 Guide
content:
Manta has exactly a handful of rooftop bars — and yes, we run one of them, so read this with that in mind. Below: every rooftop worth your evening, real opening hours, what cocktails cost, and the 30-minute sunset window you shouldn't miss. And to answer the question that brought you here: yes, the Pacific sunset really is that good. The details below decide whether you watch it from the right seat.

Quick context if you just landed: Manta is a working port city on Ecuador's central coast — the tuna capital of the eastern Pacific. The visitor zone runs from Playa Murciélago and the Malecón up to Avenida Flavio Reyes, and that's where the rooftops are.

Manta's rooftop bars, compared

Hours shift with seasons and private events; these ranges were last verified in mid-2026. Two timing notes worth knowing: Oro Verde pours from 5 p.m., the earliest in town — and we open at half past noon, which makes a long lunch with a Pacific view a legitimate plan, not just a sunset one.

The sunset window: 6:15 to 6:45 p.m., every day of the year

Manta sits almost on the equator, so sunset barely moves across the calendar — no checking apps, no seasonal math. The show itself lasts about 30 minutes, from golden light to full color over the water. If you want a seat at the rail, arrive by 6:00 p.m.; on Fridays and Saturdays, book ahead.

A first-timer's game plan, 5:45 p.m. to dinner

  • 5:45 — arrive, claim the rail. The west corner faces the water straight on.
  • 6:00 — order your first cocktail before the sunset rush hits the bar.
  • 6:15–6:45 — the show. Phones out for ten minutes, then put them down; it's better live.
  • 7:00 — order food. The kitchen moves fast before the 8 p.m. dinner wave.
  • 8:30 — decide: another round up here, or a walk down the Malecón to close the night.

What drinks and food cost (in US dollars)

Ecuador's official currency is the US dollar, which makes budgeting refreshingly simple for North American visitors: no exchange-rate math, and your cash works as-is.

  • Signature cocktails at Luuma run $9.85–$13.80: Aperol spritz $13.80, Negroni $11.50, Espresso martini $10.90, Cosmopolitan $9.85
  • Food ranges $5–$18: manabita snack boards from $8.50, carbonara $13.60, grilled shrimp $15.90, fresh white fish $17.80

A sunset cocktail plus a shared appetizer lands around $20 per person. Dinner with drinks, plan $30–40.

What to order if it's your first time

Start with the manabita snack board ($8.50) — a sampler of the province's bites, and the fastest crash course in why Manabí is considered Ecuador's food heartland. If you're hungrier, the grilled shrimp ($15.90) and the fresh white fish of the day ($17.80) come from the fleet that makes this city the tuna capital — the boats are visible from the rail.

On the glass side: the Espresso martini ($10.90) is the staff pick for sunset, and the Aperol spritz ($13.80) is the most-photographed drink on the terrace. Neither will surprise a cocktail nerd; both are executed properly, which on a rooftop at golden hour is exactly what you want.

When Luuma is NOT your best option

We'd rather point you right than have you show up wrong:

  • It's Monday. We're closed. The hotel rooftops — Oro Verde and Howard Johnson — pour daily.
  • You want to dance until 2 a.m. Our weekend close is 00:30. The DJ rooftop on Flavio Reyes runs Thursday through Saturday until 2:00.
  • You want toes-in-the-sand drinks. That's the Malecón at Playa Murciélago — beach bars, not rooftops. Different night, equally good.

Ask for the rail at the west corner — that's the seat people quietly fight over at six.

Luuma floor team

Make a day of it: rooftop night, Manta day

The sunset works better as the closing scene of a full day than as a stand-alone stop. A shape that visitors keep repeating back to us:

  • Morning: Playa Murciélago for swimming and people-watching — or Santa Marianita, 20 minutes south, if you want to watch the kitesurfers work the wind
  • Lunch: Tarqui's seafood stalls, where the fishing fleet sells straight to the kitchens — this is the cheapest great ceviche in the city
  • Late afternoon: walk the Malecón as the heat breaks
  • 6:00 p.m.: rooftop. You know the rest.

Our full guides to choosing your beach and the city's food scene go deeper — in Spanish, but nothing your browser can't translate.

Weather: does the rooftop plan ever fail?

Rarely — Manta sits in one of the driest pockets of the Ecuadorian coast. December to May is the warm, humid season with occasional afternoon bursts that clear before evening; June to November runs cooler and breezier, with grey mornings that almost always open up by sunset. Evenings hover around 22–25 °C year-round. Bring a light layer for the June–November breeze at the rail, and that's the whole weather briefing.

Getting there and practical notes

  • Luuma sits in the Flavio Reyes zone, a short taxi ride from the Malecón and Playa Murciélago
  • Fastest way to book is WhatsApp — see the button below; English is fine
  • Cards are accepted; small bills help for taxis
  • Tarqui, the old market district, is a daytime destination — go there for a $4 seafood lunch, not at night
  • The Flavio Reyes–Malecón corridor stays busy and lit in the evening; normal city precautions apply

FAQ: rooftop bars in Manta, Ecuador

Do I need a reservation?

Weekdays, walking in works. Friday and Saturday sunset slots fill up — message ahead and ask for the rail.

What time does the sun set in Manta?

Between 6:15 and 6:45 p.m. all year round. Equator perks.

Can I pay in US dollars?

It IS the local currency. Cards work at sit-down places like ours; keep small bills for taxis and street food.

Is Manta safe at night?

The visitor corridor — Flavio Reyes, the Malecón, Barbasquillo — stays busy in the evening. Standard city precautions apply, and save Tarqui for lunchtime.

Should I tip?

Sit-down restaurants in Ecuador typically include a 10% service charge in the bill, so check your receipt before doubling up. Anything you add on top of that goes straight to the team and is appreciated — but never expected. Taxis don't expect tips at all; rounding up is plenty.

Where should I go after sunset?

Our guides to Manta's nightlife and which beach to pick are in Spanish, but your browser's translate button handles them fine. Or just ask our floor team — pointing visitors somewhere good is half the job.

Book a rail seat for sunset

Message us on WhatsApp (+593 96 348 5983) and tell us how many you are and what day. If you want the west-corner rail for sunset, say so — we'll do our best. Menu and full drink list at our rooftop page.
